ambiguityScan.note: The fix's expected behaviour admits one reading. The two orderings do not compete: a filter change after a page change resets to page 1 (GH-1 AC6), and a page change after a filter change lands on page 2 of the filtered list (GH-1 AC1). Two rapid writes to different keys both land; two to the same key resolve last-write-wins, which is what the user's second action asked for. #3 carries no Gherkin because ticket-standard has no bug variant - a known gap in that standard - so the acceptance criteria are derived in the spec from GH-1's AC1 and AC6, which are the ACs the defect contradicts.

scopeChanges.change: Replace the pending-write tracking with a read of the router's live location via UNSAFE_NavigationContext, accepting a dependency on a private react-router export.
scopeChanges.why: Round 2's blocker B1 is unfixable by tracking - measured: a Back returning to the entry a write was issued from leaves the committed search, location.key and useNavigationType() all unchanged, so an abandoned write cannot be told from one in flight. Reading the live location answers both cases and deletes the ref, queue and effect entirely. Contained by a tested fallback to the committed params and a test asserting the live read, so a react-router upgrade fails a test naming the file instead of resurfacing as a URL bug.

round2.confirmed: All five round-1 blocker closures verified independently, including re-performing the unwire mutation (2 failed / 244 passed, exactly the two race guards). StrictMode soundness re-probed. Baselines re-measured and matching.
round2.blocker: B1 - a Back that lands on the pre-write URL left the write pending, and the next write resurrected the abandoned filter. Reproduced in jsdom. A regression against pre-fix behaviour, in the same window class GH-3 exists to fix.
round2.overstatedClaimFound: The round-1 record claimed 'deleting the drain, the length check, or the unchanged-URL guard each fails a different test'. Deleting the matched-commit drain (the slice) in fact failed nothing - I had mutation-tested the external-branch clear, not the slice, and wrote the claim as though it covered both. The reviewer was right; the mechanism it described no longer exists.

resolution.change: Replace the pending-write tracking entirely with a read of the router's live location through UNSAFE_NavigationContext.
resolution.why: B1 cannot be fixed by tracking. Measured: the POP returns to the identical history entry, so the committed search, location.key and useNavigationType() are all unchanged, making an abandoned write indistinguishable from one in flight by anything React has committed. The live location answers both cases correctly - during the race it reads write 1's URL, after an abandoned write plus Back it reads the popped URL. The whole ref/queue/effect mechanism is deleted with it, so B1, decision-6, decision-7 and nit-1 all cease to exist rather than being patched.
resolution.cost: UNSAFE_NavigationContext is a private react-router export and a live location on its navigator is not a documented guarantee. Contained by a documented fallback to the committed params (degrades to pre-fix behaviour, never throws) and by a test asserting the live read directly, so an upgrade fails a test naming this file. Chosen by JB Mccallaghan over documenting the residue or owning the history object via unstable_HistoryRouter (7 test files).
resolution.verification: The B1 guard fails against the pending-write mechanism from cda1c03 with exactly the value review reported (?search=login&page=2 where ?page=2 is required), so it pins the class and not just this implementation. Three mutations on the new design each killed by the right tests. E2E 82/82 twice at the new mechanism.

blockers: 1. The GH-3 fix is unguarded: unwiring the hook from TicketsPage (latest.read() -> params, noteWritten deleted) leaves the whole client suite at 239/239 and both target E2E scenarios passing. The six hook tests pass because the hook file itself is untouched - they test the hook, never that the page uses it.

2. My claim that the race is not reproducible in jsdom is FALSE. My probe used two SEQUENTIAL fireEvents, which act-flushes between; wrapping both in ONE act() reproduces it exactly - as committed gives ?sortBy=subject&sortOrder=asc&page=2, unwired gives ?page=2. So a real race guard is possible, and the justification written into two test files for not having one does not hold.
3. The spec declares an e2e/ change (the intermediate-URL assertion separating the two competing readings) and the diff touches no file under e2e/. The spec's own Open question is still unseparated.
4. No checks.e2e record at T2, despite the anti-regression plan requiring a full run with CASE-8e3d236b21a9 green and CASE-e51a15eb56e6 reported.
5. The GH-3 spec, recon and state file are all untracked - the code shipped with no committed spec, recon, check record or scope-change trail.
decisionNeeded: 6. Deleting `pending.current = null` fails no test: pending would stay non-null forever after the first write, so the adopt-external branch never runs again and Back/Forward/reload are ignored for the component's life. Missing case: write -> commit -> external change adopted.

7. The documented 'known bound' is worse than pre-fix, not neutral: on a POP during an in-flight write, latest pins the written value and the next write resurrects a filter the user navigated away from. Pre-fix wrote the popped value. Fix: clear pending on POP or key it on location.key.

8. keepPreviousData leaves the footer and rows disagreeing with no loading affordance - 'Showing 11-20 of 50' above page 1's rows, 0 skeletons - and the skeleton branch is now dead outside first mount. Neither isFetching nor isPlaceholderData is consumed.
9. CASE-93514dfd0070's move to ?page=3 is legitimate (verified by isolation) but GH-1-cases.md still states the old expectation and spec AC-d still says the case 'stays green' on that old definition.
10. The spec still says TicketsTable.tsx is not changed, while the diff changes it; the scope changes live only in the uncommitted state file.
11. AC-a/AC-b/AC-c are proven only by serialised tests, which the spec explicitly ruled out; AC-c's 'in the same render' half has no test at all.
